newsitem.title: USA: Conn. high winds cause 44,400 power outages.
newsitem.headline: Conn. high winds cause 44,400 power outages.

text.p: Wind gusts of up to 50 miles per hour caused 44,400 power outages around Connecticut on Thursday, a Northeast Utilities spokeswoman said.
Most of the outages were in the central part of the state, which had 27,500 outages as of 1730 EST, spokeswoman Sara Ellison said.
The eastern region had 1,020 outages, while there were 2,904 in northeast Connecticut. Fairfield County in southwestern Connecticut had 12,044 outages, Ellison said.
The northwest part of the state had 917 outages.
"We have a number of poles broken, that's what's going to take a bit of time to get back," Ellison said. "The cross arms are broken too."
"While we're fortunate that the trees don't have leaves, we do have a fair number of wires down."
Weather forecasts called for winds of 30-40 mph all night.
"We will continue to see outages," Ellison said. "We've had so much rain that the ground is soft and those trips tip."
